identity.intent: An intimate smoke-dark glass workshop where a tiny living amber beam remains the clearest moving subject and state reads from structure before hue.

principles.statement: One living amber light is always the first moving subject.
principles.rationale: A dark separation stroke, hot core, contact facets, and leading mote keep direction and contact readable over every material.

principles.statement: Important state differences use aperture, continuity, separation, fill, and value before color.
principles.rationale: The puzzle remains legible in desaturation and does not ask labels to carry mechanical meaning.

principles.statement: Godot owns input, orientation, state, and beam topology; painterly assets provide material specificity beneath it.
principles.rationale: Static art cannot drift from simulation, obscure a transition, or bake one topology into a reusable layer.

principles.statement: Every transformable mirror layer shares the authoritative cell center and full-cell hit region.
principles.rationale: A single pivot prevents rotation drift and preserves exact direct manipulation at 88 pixels per cell.

principles.statement: Finish the representative finale and the minimum first-puzzle reuse proof before expanding the asset vocabulary.
principles.rationale: Production feasibility is established by a running interaction, not by speculative breadth or concept art.

typography.provenance: Godot 4 engine-bundled fallback sans; no host font dependency

compatibilityDisplay.scope: unfinished title and won surfaces only

material.bench: Topology-neutral ImageGen raster, runtime-darkened, broad soot and wood wear only
material.brass: Painterly atlas patina plus native rails, pivots, and crisp value edges
material.glass: Irregular smoke-blue atlas insert plus native pale orientation spine
material.shadow: Shallow local contact shadow with no global bloom, fog, or particles
material.beam: Native CanvasItem geometry only; never a bitmap path

motion.captureSampling: Elapsed seconds advance the same presentation update as live play; no capture-only reveal fraction or semantic state is assigned
motion.authority: Simulation state changes before nonblocking presentation settles

accessibility.textureRule: Low contrast below all semantic overlays

patterns.intent: Seat a reusable painterly instrument in the workbench while preserving exact gameplay semantics.
rules: Draw native contact shadow, painterly brass mount, centered painterly insert, native orientation/focus/state geometry, then the beam.
Rotate inserts around cell_center(cell) and keep the full 88 by 88 cell as the hit target.
Use atlas pixels for material only; derive every interactive state from simulated state.

patterns.intent: Make sensor contact and shutter persistence immediately legible without a dashboard.
rules: Render the cold sensor as a hollow dark aperture and contact as a filled bright aperture with a square contour.
Render the closed shutter as one continuous blocking member and open as two retracted halves with an empty center.
Update authoritative latch state immediately, then switch its visible contact and open forms when the live beam reveal reaches the sensor.
Keep the split shutter visible during the open-but-incomplete state.
avoid: OPEN or CLOSED labels as primary evidence

patterns.intent: Preserve direction, contact, travel, and arrival over textured workshop materials.
rules: Keep the route amber before and after arrival.
Use a dark separation stroke, restrained aura, narrow hot core, contact facets, and leading mote.
Restart the 0.42 second visual reveal from normal recompute timing and begin the 0.12 second receiver settle only after full travel.
Express arrival through the receiver aperture and value response.

patterns.intent: Keep chrome subordinate to the puzzle while preserving obvious manipulation and reset.
rules: Show puzzle title, one-sentence lesson, level position, turn legend, arrow/Tab focus hint, focus feedback, and reset.
Use the right-side negative space for one restrained control surface.
Keep reset visually distinct and immediately available.
examples: BENCH CONTROL turn and focus legends

references.role: Running Godot production target at the shipping camera
Painterly brass and glass implementation atlas
references.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: layered 2D Godot game sprite atlas
Primary request: create exactly four isolated hand-painted top-down game components arranged as a precise two-by-two atlas on a perfectly flat solid #00ff00 chroma-key background.
Subject: top-left is one circular aged-brass instrument mount with an empty center; top-right is one slim imperfect hand-blown smoke-blue glass reflector blade with an opaque crisp silhouette, shown vertically; bottom-left is one compact aged-brass firefly emitter collar with a tiny warm amber glass seat but no emitted beam; bottom-right is one cool moonlit receiver housing with an empty dark aperture but no arrived state.
Style/medium: polished painterly 2D game sprites, tactile gouache and restrained impasto, orthographic top-down view, low-frequency hand-authored irregularity, production-readable at 88 pixels per game cell.
Composition/framing: exact equal quadrants in a two-by-two atlas; one centered component per quadrant; identical apparent scale; generous padding; no overlap.
Color palette: oxidized umber brass, smoke charcoal, muted blue-cyan glass, tiny warm amber seat; never use green inside a component.
Materials/textures: gently hammered aged brass, restrained verdigris pinpricks, imperfect hand-blown glass edge, soft internal value variation; crisp outer silhouettes.
Constraints: the background must be one perfectly uniform #00ff00 color with no shadows, gradients, texture, reflections, floor plane, lighting variation, or seams; no cast shadows; no contact shadows; no text; no watermark; no logos; no border; no grid; no beam or light path; no focus ring; no orientation indicator; no sensor state; no shutter; no receiver fill; no extra objects.

Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: 2D game workshop backdrop material
Primary request: an empty, smoke-dark glassworker's bench surface viewed perfectly straight down, suitable as a quiet full-screen background behind a precise puzzle board.
Scene/backdrop: one broad charcoal-blackened workbench slab with a restrained inset frame, subtle hand-rubbed soot, old scoring scratches, and faint edge-worn umber; no objects and no puzzle topology.
Style/medium: polished painterly 2D game environment layer, tactile gouache and low-frequency brushwork, intimate handmade workshop specificity, designed to remain quiet at 1152x720 gameplay scale.
Composition/framing: wide 16:10 landscape; central and left-middle areas calm and low contrast; slightly darker edges; a modest right-side recess for controls without forming a card or panel.
Lighting/mood: nocturnal workshop, extremely restrained warm grazing light from upper left and cool moonlit ambient lift from lower right; no dramatic spotlight.
Color palette: smoke charcoal, carbon black, muted umber, tiny traces of aged brass warmth and moonlit slate; near-black overall.
Materials/textures: dense dark hardwood or compressed charcoal bench, burnished worn edge, soot, hand-scored construction marks; broad low-frequency variation only.
Constraints: no text; no watermark; no logo; no grid; no cells; no beam; no glowing paths; no instruments; no receiver; no controls; no props; no shelves; no hands; no particles; no fog; no bloom; no topology-specific marks; avoid high-contrast scratches or bright focal elements.

metadata.evidenceBoundary: Running captures and deterministic scenarios establish implementation feasibility and gameplay stability, not human evidence of fun.
